LESSON: ORAL EXPRESSIONS

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: MANDARIN
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.6: Oral Expressions

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Oral Expressions. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can we practise proper articulation in communication?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. practise Oral Expressions clearly and confidently
2. use correct words and sentences for the grade level
3. give examples from school and home conversations
4. check your work for clarity and neatness

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: ORAL EXPRESSIONS
Subject: MANDARIN · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Oral Expressions helps you succeed in MANDARIN. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school and at home in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: ORAL EXPRESSIONS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Practise Oral Expressions clearly and confidently

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Oral Expressions clearly and confidently. You will use ideas from at school and at home in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Oral Expressions clearly and confidently.
2. Read, practise, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain “Oral Expressions” in your own words using one local example.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Oral Expressions clearly and confidently. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use correct words and sentences for the grade level

What this means
In this part you learn to use correct words and sentences for the grade level. You will use ideas from at school and at home in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use correct words and sentences for the grade level.
2. Read, practise, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Show one correct way to practise Oral Expressions.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use correct words and sentences for the grade level. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Give examples from school and home conversations

What this means
In this part you learn to give examples from school and home conversations. You will use ideas from at school and at home in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give examples from school and home conversations.
2. Read, practise, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give examples from school and home conversations. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Check your work for clarity and neatness

What this means
In this part you learn to check your work for clarity and neatness. You will use ideas from at school and at home in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: check your work for clarity and neatness.
2. Read, practise, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain “Oral Expressions” in your own words using one local example.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can check your work for clarity and neatness. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Oral Expressions is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Explain “Oral Expressions” in your own words using one local example. (skill: practise Oral Expressions clearly and confidently)

Example 2: Show one correct way to practise Oral Expressions. (skill: use correct words and sentences for the grade level)

Example 3: Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson. (skill: give examples from school and home conversations)

Example 4: Explain “Oral Expressions” in your own words using one local example. (skill: check your work for clarity and neatness)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Oral Expressions to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: practise Oral Expressions clearly and confidently.
3. Practise this skill: use correct words and sentences for the grade level.
4. Practise this skill: give examples from school and home conversations.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Oral Expressions from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Oral Expressions: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Oral Expressions?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we practise proper articulation in communication?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Oral Expressions means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: practise Oral Expressions clearly and confidently.
5. Be able to: use correct words and sentences for the grade level.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
